question: A 26-year-old female comes to the outpatient department with complaints of bilateral lower limb weakness and urinary incontinence for 3 days. She has a history of painful vision loss in the left eye a year ago which resolved on its own within few days. On examination, she has spastic paraparesis with sensory loss from the toes up to the level of the umbilicus. On funduscopic examination, there is optic atrophy on the left side. An MRI is ordered and T2 imaging shows areas of hyperintensities around the lateral ventricles and a post-contrast T1 sequence reveals a large hyperintense lesion in the spinal cord at the T8 level. The rest of the systemic examination was unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
